::: {#sol-bikeshare-negative}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
# `bike`, `pois_r` and `pois_py` come from the solution to the fit exercise.
# Linear regression on the same covariates as the Poisson model.
lin_r <- lm(bikers ~ temp + workingday + weathersit, data = bike)

# Count the hours whose fitted value is below zero, for each model.
fitted_lin_r <- fitted(lin_r)
fitted_pois_r <- fitted(pois_r)
n_neg_lin_r <- sum(fitted_lin_r < 0)
n_neg_pois_r <- sum(fitted_pois_r < 0)
c(linear = n_neg_lin_r, poisson = n_neg_pois_r)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
# `bike`, `pois_r` and `pois_py` come from the solution to the fit exercise.
# Linear regression on the same covariates as the Poisson model.
lin_py = smf.ols(
    "bikers ~ temp + workingday + C(weathersit, Treatment('clear'))",
    data=bike,
).fit()

# Count the hours whose fitted value is below zero, for each model.
n_neg_lin_py = int((lin_py.fittedvalues < 0).sum())
n_neg_pois_py = int((pois_py.fittedvalues < 0).sum())
{"linear": n_neg_lin_py, "poisson": n_neg_pois_py}
```

:::

The [linear regression](correlation-regression.qmd#def-linear-regression) gives a negative [fitted value](prediction.qmd#def-fitted-value) for `r n_neg_lin_r` hours,
which is impossible for the [expected value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation) of a count.

The [Poisson regression model](poisson-regression.qmd#def-poisson-regression) gives a negative fitted value for `r n_neg_pois_r` hours,
because its [event rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-event-rate) is the [exponential function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-exponential-function) of a [linear function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-linear-function),
and the exponential function takes only positive values.

:::
